about: Concept IDs and manual checks of the Ontology as Specification approach, generated by gen-approach.mjs from its ontology and catalogue. Copy it with the tool.

manualChecks.given: a term is renamed
manualChecks.then: the ID is the same and only the row's text changed

manualChecks.given: a note under a definition table
manualChecks.then: it adds detail and does not restate the definition

manualChecks.given: a new definition row
manualChecks.then: it says what the thing is in a sentence or two, not how it is stored

manualChecks.given: a rule, invariant or action that involves several entities
manualChecks.then: it sits with the entity it constrains or changes

manualChecks.given: a slice of code, the mockup included
manualChecks.when: a reviewer compares it with the ontology
manualChecks.then: everything it does is stated by a definition row or a check; what is not becomes a check or a question before the slice is done

manualChecks.given: a view or an action
manualChecks.when: a reviewer reads its rows and its checks
manualChecks.then: what the view shows in each state, what the user can do there and every outcome of the action are stated; layout and style are not asked for

manualChecks.given: a change that alters what the product does
manualChecks.then: the ontology's rows or checks change in the same change or before the code

manualChecks.given: a new entry
manualChecks.then: it answers one question; a part that answers another question is its own entry

manualChecks.given: a new entry that touches something an earlier entry decided
manualChecks.then: the new entry only adds and the earlier one stays in force, or it supersedes the earlier one whole on its `Supersedes:` line

manualChecks.given: a rule in the ontology that looks arbitrary without its reason
manualChecks.then: it names the decision by number

manualChecks.given: a new entry
manualChecks.then: it is a choice someone working on the product needs to know

manualChecks.given: an entry whose value an agent picked after being asked to tune the model
manualChecks.then: the entry is tentative until the owner accepts it

manualChecks.given: a change of the default values of a model
manualChecks.then: it is a short entry about the topic of the values, tentative when an agent chose them; a setting tuned toward a requirement has no entry

manualChecks.given: a new entry
manualChecks.then: it says why, and lists the rejected alternatives with their reasons

manualChecks.given: an entry that replaces an earlier one
manualChecks.then: it names the entries it supersedes

manualChecks.given: a change to the ontology that rests on a choice
manualChecks.then: a decision entry records the choice

manualChecks.given: the owner's message and an answer a colleague gave for the owner disagree about one choice
manualChecks.then: it follows the owner's message and names it on its `Source:` line; an entry resting only on the colleague's answer is tentative

manualChecks.given: a question with options and a recommendation
manualChecks.then: it is a tentative entry whose decision is the recommendation and whose rejected alternatives are the other options, not a line under open questions

manualChecks.given: a tentative entry or an open question waits for the owner
manualChecks.then: it asks what no run can settle; a question about speed, fit or behavior carries the result of a prototype instead of waiting

manualChecks.given: the owner answers a tentative entry
manualChecks.then: the entry is accepted as written or as rewritten to the chosen option and names the answer on its `Source:` line, and History records the acceptance; the entry of a dropped question is removed, and History says so

manualChecks.given: something is put off: a target concept or an item out of scope
manualChecks.then: an entry defers it with a `Return when:` line

manualChecks.given: a change to behavior
manualChecks.then: the implementation table changed in the same change, and the note of a partial row names the target concept that adds what is missing

manualChecks.given: a row of the implementation table
manualChecks.when: a reviewer opens the files it names
manualChecks.then: they realise the concept

manualChecks.given: code that implements a concept
manualChecks.then: an `ont:` comment next to the code names the concept

manualChecks.given: a blind walk found that renewal goes through while someone waits, that the hold queue is not served, and that nothing says what a damaged item shows
manualChecks.then: the walker had no access to the code; the renewal became a known divergence, the case of the damaged item a check, and the queue nothing new, since it is target

manualChecks.given: a new line under known divergences
manualChecks.then: it describes behavior that contradicts the target, not something missing

manualChecks.given: a known divergence
manualChecks.then: it points at a ticket or a pending decision, and neither side was edited to hide it

manualChecks.given: the mockup
manualChecks.when: a reviewer opens it from the file system
manualChecks.then: there is one mockup for the product, it runs without a build, and it shows the target

manualChecks.given: a mockup shared outside the team
manualChecks.then: it holds no real names or records

manualChecks.given: an element labelled with an action
manualChecks.when: a person uses it in the mockup
manualChecks.then: it does what the action's definition says

manualChecks.given: the map
manualChecks.then: it is grouped by screen with one row per element

manualChecks.given: an element the mockup deliberately leaves without some behavior, such as a button that is never offered
manualChecks.when: a reviewer looks for the reason
manualChecks.then: the ontology states it, in a definition, a note of the screen or the out-of-scope list, and the map does not

manualChecks.given: a new check
manualChecks.then: it names members, items and dates from the sample, and no function, command or selector

manualChecks.given: a manual check that could not be run
manualChecks.then: it says not run, and the evidence of the checks that ran is kept by check and date

manualChecks.given: a decision that chooses a value, a requirement or the assumptions of a model
manualChecks.then: an automatic check holds the value or the requirement; for the model, a check holds a snapshot of its base scenario's results, and none requires it to reach its goal

manualChecks.given: a judged check of a summary the product writes
manualChecks.then: the judge gets the check's case and the summary, and neither the code nor an expected text

manualChecks.given: a judged check that ran
manualChecks.then: its verdict is kept outside the repository, named by the check and the date

manualChecks.given: two checks of `action.renew` whose cases differ only in the member and the title
manualChecks.then: one of them goes

manualChecks.given: a case the catalogue does not hold, with the owner's answer kept outside the catalogue
manualChecks.when: someone who sees only the ontology and the catalogue says what should happen
manualChecks.then: it matches the owner's answer; a mismatch adds a check, or an open question when the owner does not know the answer

manualChecks.given: a review of a change in a project that sets `manualRuns`
manualChecks.when: a reviewer looks for its records
manualChecks.then: every verdict of the review has a record, and each record that needs evidence links to it outside the repository

manualChecks.given: a tagged test
manualChecks.when: a reviewer reads it with its check
manualChecks.then: it sets up GIVEN, does WHEN and asserts THEN

manualChecks.given: a ticket
manualChecks.then: it lists concepts and checks; any behavior it needs is already in the catalogue

manualChecks.given: an agent looks for work
manualChecks.then: the slice holds ready targets only, cut into a ticket from `--next`; a target that waits for the owner is left until the owner answers

manualChecks.given: the tickets open in a project
manualChecks.then: each is being worked on now; none was cut ahead to hold concepts for later, and an agent that cut one did only what the owner allows

manualChecks.given: a ticket whose `--gap` prints `SLICE_DONE` and whose tests pass
manualChecks.then: it is closed, and its file or its tracker entry is still there

manualChecks.given: several agents start work at the same time, each on a branch of its own
manualChecks.when: a reviewer reads the tickets they work from
manualChecks.then: one coordinator cut them all, they were on the main branch before the agents started, and no concept is in two of them

manualChecks.given: a ticket cut from what `--next` proposed
manualChecks.when: a reviewer reads the change that closes it
manualChecks.then: it is one change the reviewer can follow with its tests; if not, the ticket should have been split along the dependencies, the part the rest depends on first

manualChecks.given: the agent rules section
manualChecks.then: it fits on one screen and every row names a path or a command

manualChecks.given: a task for an agent
manualChecks.then: it names the IDs the task touches before writing code

manualChecks.given: a consistency review of a project
manualChecks.then: each one says who would be misled or which check would break; style, list completeness and compliance that changes nothing are left out

manualChecks.given: an agent accepted a decision entry as part of a change
manualChecks.then: the change is in a commit of its own files and no one else's, so the guard protects the entry; whether the commit or a push waited for an approval is the user's choice

manualChecks.given: a change to a rule of the approach
manualChecks.then: the reviewer did not write it and got the diff and the IDs it touches, not the author's conclusions

manualChecks.given: a process rule in the agent instructions, such as one that says agents do not commit
manualChecks.then: it names the rule of the approach or the entry it comes from, and a rule that departs from the approach cites a process entry that extends or overrides it. The tool cannot tell a process rule from a command or a matter of style, nor whether a rule written in prose is stricter or looser than the approach

manualChecks.given: an agent was corrected for a mistake it could make again
manualChecks.when: a reviewer reads the change that holds the correction
manualChecks.then: it is held by the structure of the code, a check, a test or a lint where one of them can hold it; a rule in the agent instructions only where none can, and the rule says so

manualChecks.given: a change about to be merged
manualChecks.when: a reviewer looks for its review
manualChecks.then: an agent of another provider that did not write it gave each check `--review` listed a verdict, and a check it could not run is `not run` with the reason, not `not applicable`

manualChecks.given: a page of a doc set
manualChecks.then: every section that explains a concept has an anchor, and none copies a definition

manualChecks.given: sections listed to reread
manualChecks.then: they reread each section first and fixed what changed

manualChecks.given: a section of a run guide
manualChecks.when: someone who has not seen the product follows it
manualChecks.then: they run the check, and the section names the check without restating its case

manualChecks.given: a profile
manualChecks.then: everything it requires is enforced through the configuration and the catalogue, and the rest is listed as recommended
